commentary: Today Iron ore futures trended weaker with the most-traded contract I2609 closed at 803 yuan/mt, down 1.11% from the previous trading session. Port spot prices were 2-4 yuan higher than the previous day. Traders showed moderate enthusiasm in oﬀering; steel mill purchases were mostly driven by rigid demand; overall spot trading senƟment was lukewarm. Last week, SMM global iron ore shipments totaled 30.922 million mt, up 5.48% WoW. Among them, Australian shipments were basically stable, while Brazil's shipments rebounded signiﬁcantly. In addiƟon, last week, total iron ore arrivals at Chinese ports reached 25.9288 million mt, up 5% WoW and up 6.28% YoY on a cumulaƟve basis. Iron ore fundamentals conƟnued last week's paƩern. Supply side, as mainstream mines accelerated shipments in Q2, there were again signs of entering a loosening channel. However, demand side, blast furnace operaƟng rates remained at relaƟvely high levels, ensuring rigid demand for iron ore. Therefore, iron ore's upside was relaƟvely limited, but price support remained generally solid. On the macro front, coking coal and coke prices fell on futures due to a policy shiŌ, dragging overall ferrous metals prices weaker. However, given that iron ore's own fundamental price support remained relaƟvely ﬁrm, iron ore prices are expected to resume ﬂuctuaƟng at highs aŌer a brief pullback this week.
